failure_modes.cause: Single point of failure for pressure control; blockage by precipitates or mechanical failure leads to uncontrolled pressure rise or flow stoppage
failure_modes.mitigation: Install redundant pressure relief valve (PRV) set at 2.5 bar and implement real-time pressure monitoring with auto-shutdown

failure_modes.mode: Pump cavitation due to insufficient NPSH
failure_modes.cause: At 60°C, solvent vapour pressure increases; if feed reservoir is not pressurised, inlet pressure may drop below vapour pressure causing cavitation and flow instability
failure_modes.mitigation: Pressurise feed reservoir to 0.5 bar above solvent vapour pressure at 60°C and use low-pulsation syringe pumps

failure_modes.mode: Incomplete quenching leading to exothermic runaway
failure_modes.cause: Quench required but mixing efficiency in laminar regime (Re=13) may be insufficient for rapid quench, risking post-reactor exotherm
failure_modes.mitigation: Validate quench mixing efficiency via tracer study and ensure quench reagent is in excess with rapid static mixer post-reactor

single_points_of_failure: BPR valve — blockage stops all flow
Single pump — failure halts entire process
validation_experiments: Run blank solvent at Q=0.45 mL/min for 60 min; monitor pressure for drift > 5% to verify BPR stability
Perform quench efficiency test using a fast model reaction (e.g., acid-base neutralisation with pH indicator) to confirm mixing adequacy
Simulate pump failure by stopping flow and monitoring pressure relief valve activation and system depressurisation time
